title: Children's Room Design: Key Principles | DUMSKAYA DESIGN
description: How to design a child's room: safety, zoning, furniture that grows with the child, light and colour. Key rules from DUMSKAYA DESIGN.

parts.html: In a children’s room, safety, functionality, and aesthetics are especially important. Here are the basic rules that will help you take everything into account.
Age: The needs of an infant, a preschooler, and a school-age child differ greatly. Keep in mind that a toddler needs more room to play, while a schoolchild needs a place to study.
Interests: Take your child’s hobbies into account: a room like that is inspiring and comfortable to be in.
Zoning: Divide the room into zones for sleeping, playing, and studying.
Functionality: Make sure each zone serves its purpose. For example, the sleeping area should be calm and dark, while the play area should be bright and safe.
Ergonomics: Choose furniture to suit your child’s height: a desk and chair appropriate for their age, and shelves within easy reach.
Color palette: Keep the main finishes in calm, neutral colors and add bright accents with decor and textiles. Bright colors suit the play area; calm ones suit the sleeping area.
Lighting:
Natural light: Let as much daylight into the room as possible.
General lighting: Create even lighting with ceiling fixtures.
Zone lighting: Add reading lamps next to the bed, as well as a desk lamp on the desk.
Materials: Use eco-friendly, hypoallergenic materials. This is especially important for wall finishes, flooring, and furniture.
Furniture: Avoid sharp corners and check that large pieces are stable. If your child is young, be sure to anchor cabinets and shelves to the walls.
Electrical: Fit all outlets with safety covers and hide the cables.
Bed: For toddlers, choose beds with side rails to prevent falls. For school-age children, beds with storage drawers are a good fit.
Storage: Plan storage systems for toys, clothes, and books. Modules that can easily be rearranged and adapted as your child grows are ideal.
Multifunctional furniture: If space is tight, choose furniture that serves several purposes — for example, a bed with a work area or a folding table.
Textiles: Add soft elements — cushions, rugs, curtains. They not only make the room cozier but also bring in pops of color.
Personalization: Your child should feel that the room is truly theirs. Use their favorite colors and add decor featuring their favorite characters or motifs.
Modularity: Keep in mind that your child’s needs will change. Use modular systems that can easily be adapted to new purposes.
Room to grow: Leave some free space so you can add new elements over time, such as a study area or extra storage.
Details: Add interesting details that highlight your child’s personality: shelves with their favorite books, an art wall for painting or a magnetic board.
Inspiration: Draw ideas from magazines and interior design websites, but adapt them to your child’s real needs and preferences.
A good children’s room is more than just a furnished room — it’s a space that helps your child grow, inspires them, and brings them joy.
